correctness.rationale: Wang et al. eqs. (6), (22)–(33) give the stated block matrix and positive-weight linearization; eqs. (5), (16)–(17) have no commuting parameter at the disease-free equilibrium. The diagonal similarity is valid for every positive Theta. Nonnegativity identifies the spectral radius with the top eigenvalue of the symmetric similar matrix, so a maximum of affine Rayleigh quotients gives the chord and convex strict sublevel set, without irreducibility. The city-constant quotient eigenvector is strictly positive for sigma>0 by the positive cross-block row sums; the componentwise Collatz–Wielandt bounds give equality with the full radius, and at zero the two blocks separate. For a≠e, the square-root term has positive curvature on the open interval; L'(0+) is 0 if a<e and −a if a>e. For a=e the slope is positive directly. For a>e the stationary equations give the stated sigma* and L*; the candidate satisfies L*>e and hence is on the upper branch, and if sigma*≥1 there is no interior turning point. The final negative-derivative sentence in Step 3 inherits the a>e case, not a≤e. An independent exact finite witness check in /workspace/branches/d7ad5a18-357a-4741-9ffe-86fc016b8e97/ordinal-3-spectral-witness-check.md checks dimensions, cross-incidence connectivity, the full root via the positive quotient lift, and exact signs/crossings. In the source map the all-unaware equilibrium is admissible: zero pairwise acquisition leaves at most quadratic acquisition, and the active/removed first-order block is triangular with both decay multipliers below one. No supplied code was executed. Conclusions concern the linearized map only; the endpoints are neutral in the leading mode, not classified nonlinearly.

value.rationale: The source reports that threshold behavior can vary with network structure. The general barrier rules out one order of signs for every fixed-weight network, while the regular-class criterion and exact graph establish rigorously that the opposite order is possible under the asymmetric-city constraints. This distinction is more informative than fitting a nonmonotone simulation or merely restating the Perron threshold. No inference to actual commuting policies or global extinction is warranted.
